extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and counsel in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and required contents/procedures for accepting an affidavit of resignation (exclusion on consent) under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and related USPTO disciplinary rules, and the Office's orders that flow from approval. Applies to practitioners facing disciplinary complaints who seek exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a). The Director determined Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit seeking exclusion on consent must meet the regulatory requirements in § 11.27(a) (as judged by the Director) before approval and exclusion will be ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent must be freely and voluntarily rendered
rubrics_metrics.description: The Respondent's consent is 'freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should explicitly state consent is voluntary and free from coercion; the Office will confirm voluntariness as part of determining compliance with § 11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of pending disciplinary complaint and underlying allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must be aware that a disciplinary complaint is pending and of the substance of the allegations (here: allegations culminating in pleading guilty to, and conviction of, conspiracy to commit securities fraud).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should acknowledge knowledge of the pending complaint and the factual/legal basis of the complaint so the Office can determine the respondent understood what they were surrendering by consenting to exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) — disreputable or gross misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is of the opinion that respondent's conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) (proscribing engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When alleged conduct amounts to disreputable or gross misconduct, the OED will view that as a ground relevant to disciplinary action and to acceptance of resignation on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3) via § 10.23(c)(1) — conviction of criminal offense involving moral turpitude, dishonesty, or breach of trust
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director alleges violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(1) (conviction of a criminal offense involving moral turpitude, dishonesty, or breach of trust).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal convictions involving moral turpitude or dishonesty are treated as disciplinary misconduct and are cited when evaluating appropriateness of exclusion on consent and future reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — engaging in conduct involving dishonesty
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is of the opinion that respondent engaged in conduct involving dishonesty in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of dishonest conduct are material to disciplinary proceedings and to the OED's opinion supporting exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) — conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director alleges respondent engaged in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct that undermines administration of justice is a stated ground for discipline and informs the Office's handling of resignation and exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director alleges respondent engaged in 'any other conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the USPTO' in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad catch-all provision for conduct affecting fitness to practice; may be invoked in OED opinion supporting exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.57(b)(1) — knowingly revealing a client's confidence or secret
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director alleges violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.57(b)(1) (proscribing knowingly revealing a confidence or secret of a client).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misuse or disclosure of client confidences is a specific disciplinary rule relevant to fitness and possible exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.57(b)(2) — knowingly using a client's confidence to the client's disadvantage
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director alleges violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.57(b)(2) (proscribing knowingly using a confidence or secret of a client to the disadvantage of the client).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using client confidences to the client's detriment is actionable misconduct cited by OED in disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.57(b)(3) — using client confidence for practitioner's or third party's advantage without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director alleges violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.57(b)(3) (proscribing knowingly using a confidence or secret of a client for the advantage of the practitioner or of a third person, unless the client consents after full disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should acknowledge such allegations where applicable; lack of client consent to use confidences is a disciplinary concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption on reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that, if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (i) the allegations set forth in the disciplinary complaint pending against him are true and (ii) he could not have successfully defended himself against such allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiants consenting to exclusion accept that the OED will treat the underlying allegations as true for reinstatement proceedings; this is an important consequence to be disclosed and understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiant must fully read and understand 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent 'has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60, and is fully aware of the legal and factual consequences of requesting and consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should attest to knowledge of these specific regulations and their consequences; the Office requires such acknowledgement prior to approving exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of exclusion on consent (scope and effective date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Order: Respondent's Affidavit is approved and 'Respondent shall be excluded on consent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office beginning on the date this Final Order is signed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An approved affidavit results in an express order excluding the practitioner from specified practice before the Office effective on the order date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED Reading Room and Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette (the order includes the exact notice text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of resignation on consent triggers public notice obligations: posting in OED Reading Room and publishing notice in the Official Gazette, with content identifying the practitioner, registration number, the fact of voluntary resignation while complaint pending, the alleged rule violations, and the statutes/regulations under which action was taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: The order requires that 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-exclusion duties (as set out in § 11.58) must be followed by the excluded practitioner; affidavit should reflect awareness and acceptance of these duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval of an affidavit triggers mandatory notification obligations to state agencies and courts under § 11.59; affidavits should contemplate these disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: The order recites that 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement applications are governed by § 11.60 and the respondent must follow those procedural and substantive requirements when seeking to regain eligibility to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties bear their own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The order states 'The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The approved resignation on consent does not allocate costs between the parties; each bears its own.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director to move to dismiss pending disciplinary complaint within 14 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall move to dismiss the pending disciplinary complaint within fourteen days of the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval of the affidavit triggers an obligation by OED to promptly move to dismiss the pending complaint, with a specified fourteen-day timeframe in this order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and statutory authority for action
rubrics_metrics.description: Action taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27 and 11.59. The Director has authority to approve Affidavit of Resignation and exclude respondent on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director's power to accept/exercise exclusion on consent is grounded in the cited sections of title 35 and 37 C.F.R.; filings and orders should reference these authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's registration status and scope of practice noted
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is identified as a registered patent practitioner (Registration No. 52,193) and the order notes he is a patent agent (not a patent lawyer) and therefore not entitled to practice trademark or other non-patent law before the Office, but the Final Order encompasses practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits and orders should accurately state registration number and clarify the scope of practice being affected; even agents (not attorneys) may be excluded from broader categories of practice before the Office.
